Maya: FYI we just had a reproduceable OOM on a dedicated shard when a client sent a burst of long-context chat requests with batching=4. Caused by KV slab fragmentation + decode-time prefill spikes.
Oliver: ouch. which model/quant? any flamegraphs?
Maya: rtx-8gb small-quant run, model=v1-chat-16k-quant. PerfBot posted a quick profile: https://perf.internal/runs/1758001234 (flamegraph shows many tiny free runs).
Devin: Sounds like the slab allocator is leaving a lot of <8KB holes after buffer reuse. Prefill path allocates many transient KV nodes during tokenization/embedding that aren't consolidated.
Sasha: Did the OOM happen during prefill or decode? we saw both modes behave differently in earlier runs.
Maya: It spikes in the decode window: prefill writes KV entries then decode attempts to reuse workspace buffers but allocation fails due to fragmented free lists. Reproducer command: `curl -X POST https://int-api/redwood/infer -d '{"model":"v1-chat-16k-quant","batch":4,"input":"<long chat>"}'`
Oliver: Two quick ideas: 1) per-request soft cap for KV prefill (reject/gate prefill if request would exceed), 2) opportunistic compaction when fragmentation ratio > 0.6.
Devin: Agree on soft cap. Proposed config snippet: ```json
{"kv_per_request_soft_cap_bytes": 62914560, "kv_fragmentation_threshold": 0.6, "kv_compact_window_ms": 250}
```
Sasha: Compacting during heavy load risks adding latency. Maybe do compaction only during idle slices or when decode backlog is low; otherwise evict oldest prefill entries first.
Maya: For this burst, evicting oldest prefill would have kept latency but prevented OOM. We also saw that prefills from long system messages are very sticky. Suggest eviction priority: decode-ephemeral < prefill-shortlived < prefill-longlived (LRU with weight).
Oliver: Also need to adjust kernel selection heuristics: small-fragment-heavy devices should prefer kernels that avoid extra temporary allocations (there is a comms path that creates temp KV buffers). Put a frag-penalty into kernel score.
Devin: I'll add a perf test that ramps load with alternating short/long contexts and measure fragmentation vs live-resident bytes. If frag ratio crosses threshold, test fallback path with prefill-gate enabled.
PerfBot: Allocation summary for reproducer run: total_kv_bytes=2.3GB, live_resident=1.1GB, internal_fragmentation=1.2GB (52%). Top alloc sizes: 7KB(48%), 32KB(22%), 256B(15%).
OncallBot: Incident created: INC-2025-4892, assign oncall if it recurs.
Sasha: Action items: Devin creates perf branch with: 1) per-request soft cap + metrics, 2) eviction weight change for prefill types, 3) frag-aware kernel scoring. Maya will craft repro harness with logs for free-run lengths. Oliver will prototype idle compaction guard.
Maya: thanks — will post next reproducer logs when ready. :thumbsup:
